intent:
"yes approbe and begin the implementation" started the bstack build slice by slice, strictly one at a time ("keep it sequential"). Later: "i'm only not concerned about security hardening, threat-model concerns. Style and simplification and following proper design principles are still important." - build the full app fast, but review the core properly so slices and phases do not leave bugs.

The plans of record are in the repo: `docs/design.md` (requirements and decisions, including R24: licensing is out of scope) and `docs/implementation-plan.md` (tasks, task evidence contract). knowttl/bstack is public, has no GitHub Actions or workflows and no release automation, and ships through the no-mistakes pipeline (`.no-mistakes.yaml` owns the review budget and focus) with automatic merge of green work. Phase 0 and C6a (https://github.com/knowttl/bstack/pull/11: `tests/fixtures/build.mjs` plus the new-idea, ambiguous-idea and clear-goals fixtures) have landed. The merged slice table is `[redacted: host path] (bstack table).

This piece is merged slice C6bc (old C6b + C6c), which completes task T1.1 "Build the test fixtures": the `ts-shop/` and `py-ledger/` fixtures with their seeded problems and native setup, the clean rule-proof variants for both stacks, and the dirty-work, refactor, contract-removal, shallow-history and installer-collision variants (merged done evidence: each native sanity check executes and confirms its valid and invalid seeds; deterministic dirty/refactor/history/installer seeds, clean proof variants, independent alias/cycle switches).
amendments: C6bc completes the remaining native and state fixtures on top of C6a. Evidence-only commits name the tested implementation revision.
R6 refresh records all five required commands against the final implementation revision after the rename, sanity identity and checkout repairs; this commit changes evidence only.
